The chain's in-fleet hops are all VERIFIED: F11 names the external host (api.exchange-partner.example) with 5000ms connect timeouts from 11:01:25Z plus application-layer 503s carrying the partner's own x-partner-request-id; F10/F18 show exchange-gateway's error_rate (~44%)/p99 (4811ms) jump with flat request_rate and flat CPU/memory (F31/F32), so no local saturation and no load driver; F8/F9 show every order-service error (349/350) is the identical 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' with flat local CPU and a pure downstream-wait latency profile; F25/F26/F27/F28 establish market-data-service as a second independent caller through exchange-gateway and show no deployment or config change on that path. H1 is decisively rebutted by the flat rate across the 11:16Z rollback (F19-F23) and by the pre-existing, one-hop-earlier onset. Alternatives H3 (pricing-engine error_rate AND logs clean, F16) and H4 (ledger-db clean on slow_queries, connections_active and WARN logs - multi-metric, F13/F14/F15) are properly tested and cannot generate an exchange-gateway-scoped error text. The unresolved element is INSIDE H2 - whether the origin is the partner service itself or a DNS/egress/NAT/TLS path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner - i.e. uncertainty in a secondary detail of an established origin, not a competing origin. Both readings point at the same remediation (raise/disable the 5s upstream timeout and circuit breaker, fail fast/degrade exchange-dependent submit, engage the partner), so no further query would change which hypothesis ranks first. Remaining gaps (market-data-service metrics, exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate, per-minute onset shape) would only firm up an already-established origin and are not worth minutes during an ongoing outage. Cap reflects the one untestable external hop and coarse-bucket internal ordering.

tasks.objective: Characterize the symptom: establish the exact onset time of order-service 504s/errors (before vs. after the v2.15.2 deploy time), the error signature (timeout vs. connection refused vs. 5xx from a dependency), and whether other services in the fleet show correlated error/latency spikes. Report resource trends (CPU, memory, connections/latency) for order-service and any suspect dependency over the last 6 hours.
tasks.answer: order-service's ~30% failure rate began at ~11:01-11:02Z, with the first metric bucket already saturated by 11:00Z (17.3% avg at 10:58-11:07) — the symptom is entirely a dependency-call failure: every order-service error is "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)", while order-service's own CPU (~40%) and latency baseline were flat/stable. The fails originate one hop upstream at exchange-gateway, whose own error_rate jumped 0.2% -> ~40-44% at the same 11:00Z bucket and whose logs show upstream connect timeouts (5000ms) and 503s from api.exchange-partner.example starting 11:01:25Z. This is an exchange-partner-side/upstream connectivity failure rather than a local order-service resource problem.

tasks.objective: Enumerate everything that changed in the fleet around the onset window (approx 08:00-11:10Z): all deployments and config changes across ALL services, not just order-service. Include order-service v2.15.2 details, and map order-service's upstream/downstream dependencies. Search historical incidents for prior order submit failures / 504s and their root causes.
tasks.answer: Around the onset window (08:00-11:10Z) the ONLY deployment in the fleet was order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, deployed 10:48Z, "Add idempotency keys to order submit"), already rolled back at 11:16Z. The only config change was pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5→4s at 09:20Z. No deployments or config changes occurred in the preceding ~24h. order-service depends on ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce), and is called by api-gateway; ledger-db and kafka are SHARED by other services (portfolio/payment/settlement and payment/settlement/notification), so a neighbour could hurt order-service through them. Historical precedents for "504 on order submit" exist but with different root causes (HIST-103 external exchange outage; HIST-116 gateway envoy upgrade; HIST-110 ledger-db IOPS; HIST-115 order-service pool config) - these are leads only, not evidence of the current cause.
